subject: Urgent: production 5xx/429 surge + retry amplification impacting throughput
messages:
From: Sara Cohen <sara.cohen@lumenix.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumenix Ops <ops@lumenix.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx + 429 surge (region us-west)

Hi Priya,

We saw a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses starting around 08:42 PDT this morning. Our service graph shows repeated timeouts and a retry amplification pattern: clients backing off briefly, then bunching and re-saturating your endpoint. Impact: our nightly inference job failed repeatedly (throughput dropped ~70%), and several user-facing pipelines are returning 500s.

Attached are two quick artifacts: error-log-tail.txt (last 500 lines) and p95-latency.png (30m window). The errors reference service IDs that look like GPU allocation failures and timeouts. We believe autoscaling didn't absorb the load — seeing long queue lengths with GPU pools not adding capacity fast enough.

Can you confirm whether this is a Dedicated pool autoscaling lag or something on Hosted? We are on a Dedicated reservation (LUM-RES-09) with a min capacity of 4 GPU nodes. This is causing a business outage for several paying customers. We need an ETA for mitigation and any immediate workarounds (client-side throttles, model fallbacks, region failover).

Regards,
Sara Cohen
Head of Platform Ops
Lumenix Therapeutics

Attachments:
- error-log-tail.txt (text)
- p95-latency.png (image)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx + 429 surge (region us-west)

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra team immediately. Initial plan:

- Confirm whether the Dedicated pool (LUM-RES-09) autoscaler showed lag and whether nodes were pending provisioning.
- Gather runtime metrics (GPU queue length, KV cache hit-rate, model warm-up status).
- Propose short-term mitigations: enable client-side exponential backoff (if not already), temporary model downgrade to a smaller variant we have warm in the pool, or manual increase of min nodes.

Can you share the HubSpot deal id and any SLA language that would trigger credits if this is >30m? Also sharing the request IDs that correspond to the errors will help correlate traces — are the IDs in error-log-tail.txt the full request ids?

I’ll update you within 60 minutes with the triage output or earlier if we have a mitigation.

— Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx + 429 surge (region us-west)

Sara / Priya — pushing initial findings from on-call (summary):

Observations:
- Dedicated pool LUM-RES-09 reported a rapid queue increase starting 08:35 PDT; p95 token latency climbed concurrently.
- Autoscaler actions show "scale_pending" state for ~7 minutes; infra attempted to spin up new nodes but provisioning lag (cloud AZ quota hit and image pull delays) prevented capacity entering the pool fast enough.
- Multiple model shards showed cold KV caches after the prior maintenance window; first requests load KV and cause backpressure for subsequent requests (classic cold-start amplification).
- Retry storms visible: clients with linear retry backoff were re-firing after the autoscaler window — leading to repeated bursts that drove GPUs into OOM/5xx on some nodes.

Attachments: pool-snapshot-20270530.json (pool state at 09:05 PDT), repro-requests.txt (sample requests we replayed locally that reproduce the 500s).

Immediate mitigations applied (30m):
1) Temporarily increased min nodes for LUM-RES-09 from 4 -> 8 (manual override) to buy headroom.
2) Enabled model-variant fallback route for Lumenix requests to smaller quantized model (latency tradeoff) for requests from their API key.
3) Pushed a rate-limit header enforcement gate to edge (warn only) and recommended client-side exponential backoff (max attempts 3).

Follow-ups (next 24h recommended):
- Cloud quota review with the infra team to prevent image-pull throttling.
- Tune autoscaler detection window from 180s -> 60s for this pool and add a fastpath for warm KV heuristics.
- Add warm-up prefetch for high-QPS shards before rolling maintenance.

We’re monitoring; I'll post updated metric screenshots and traces to the incident thread. If Lumenix wants a live call we can jump in — Priya, Marcus and I are available.

— Aditya Rao
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Our finance and product teams are asking about remediation credits and SLA impact. We are preparing a short executive note for our CPO and legal. Can Redwood confirm timeline for final root cause analysis, and whether there is a bill credit process that will start if we confirm a platform-side failure?

Also, can you provide a short runbook we can reference for client mitigation (recommended backoff values, model fallback configuration)?

Sara Cohen

Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx + 429 surge (region us-west) — exec summary + ask

Team — executive update to loop in leadership and finalize customer remediation:

Summary of incident (for execs):
- Start: 2027-05-30 08:35 PDT. Impact: elevated 5xx/429 rates and timeouts for Lumenix pipelines; throughput dropped ~60% for critical jobs. Root cause: combined autoscaler provisioning lag (AZ quota + image-pull delays) and cold KV cache warm-up that amplified retries into GPU OOM/5xx.

Actions taken so far:
- Manual scale from 4 -> 8 nodes; enabled fallback to smaller quantized model for Lumenix keys; recommended client-side backoff (max 3 attempts).
- Short-term autoscaler tuning (detection window reduced, fastpath added) pushed to staging; cloud quota request submitted.
- We captured diagnostic artifacts and repro requests; see related_links for incident and HubSpot deal.

Customer ask / outstanding items:
- Lumenix requests SLA credit process started and a timeline for RCA (they expect credit assessment if platform-side fault >30m).
- They asked for an exec touchpoint (CPO) — I expect Tom Alvarez to request a call if the issue persists.

Internal ask (approval):
- Approve a 10% service credit provisional offer to Lumenix while we complete RCA (escalation to finance required).
- Approve an emergency change: increase Dedicated pool min nodes permanently to 6 while autoscaler window tuning rolls out (this is temporary + revert within 72h if no further issues).
- Authorize a post-incident customer debrief (RCA) and a joint review call with Lumenix leadership.

If approved, I’ll coordinate communications and the timeline. Marcus, can you validate cloud quota ETA and whether a permanent AZ increase is feasible? Aditya, can you confirm the scheduled job to backfill KV warm caches before maintenance windows? Marissa, I’m looping you for customer success coordination and SLA credit paperwork.

Thanks — I’ll compile a one-page RCA draft once we confirm metrics and traces.

— Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
